elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 states that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable and other work product created for Customer.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 provides that Vendor hereby assigns all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable and work product to Customer.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Sections 1.4 and 14.3 exclude Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how from Deliverables and provide that Vendor retains Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Sections 14.3 and 13.2 grant a perpetual licence to Vendor Technology embedded in a Deliverable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the licence to embedded Vendor Technology irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Section 13.2 expressly makes the licence royalty-free and fully paid.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Section 14.1 states that Customer owns all Customer Data and gives Vendor only a limited processing right.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Section 14.4 states that no jointly owned intellectual property is created. Its exception requires a separate signed instrument, and no such instrument is present.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: Section 1.4 excludes Vendor Technology and generally applicable ideas, methods, skills, and know-how from Deliverables, while Section 14.3 confirms Vendor retains Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Customer owns Deliverables under Section 14.2 rather than receiving a perpetual licence to them; Section 13.2 licenses only specified software and Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: No irrevocable licence to Deliverables is granted. The irrevocable licence in Section 13.2 applies to software and Vendor Technology, not Deliverables generally.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No worldwide licence to Deliverables is granted. The worldwide language in Section 13.2 applies only to software and Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty-free licence to Deliverables is granted. The royalty-free language in Section 13.2 applies only to software and Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Customer's exclusive ownership and receipt of all right, title, and interest in Deliverables under Section 14.2 encompass use and modification without a business-use restriction.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: The rendered language does not expressly grant a sublicensing right for Deliverables. Section 13.2 only permits contractors to support licensed Vendor Technology.
